text:
anya: FYI saw a strange failure on staging: safetensors shards uploaded with gzip-but-indexed-as-raw broke our mmap hotstart.
jon: ugh. did the shard writer change? we recently flipped a pipeline flag to always gzip large chunks.
anya: yep that's the root cause. the consumers assumed index offsets map 1:1 to file offsets. gzip breaks that.
sasha: we should add a tiny handshake at load-time: a capabilities header that declares whether the artifact supports range-decompress, is mmap-friendly, and where signature/meta lives.
kevin: agreed but careful: every extra call on cold start adds p99 time. any handshake should be optional and cacheable.
claire: idea: store a lightweight .capabilities blob next to the shard blob (same naming as object + ".caps.json"). it contains fields: compression: "gzip"|"none", ranges_supported: true|false, meta_location: "sidecar"|"catalog", background_prefetch: true|false. cheap GET of .caps.json should be cheaper than a HEAD on some providers.
jon: that sounds pragmatic. we can fall back to heuristic: if .caps.json missing, try HEAD, if HEAD denies, fallback to streaming-first with conservative prefetch.
anya: loader behaviour proposal: 1) check local caps cache for model+artifact hash. 2) if miss, attempt caps read (meta blob or HEAD) with a short timeout. 3) based on flags choose path: mmap-first (index-only), stream-first (gzip-aware), or staged (start streaming low-priority warmup and concurrently try index fallback).
sasha: detail: index files need a version tag. older index v0 assumed raw offsets; v1 can include per-chunk mapping and decompress hints. loader should treat index version mismatch as an automatic caps-fallback.
kevin: we also must define verification order for signed artifacts. If sidecar signature exists, we can verify caps before transferring bulk. But some registries sign lazily and signature may be delegated to a catalog service. we need a 3-state signature enum: verified|absent|delegated.
claire: operational constraints: make caps fetch idempotent and rate-limited by artifact hash to avoid DOSing object stores on large rollout. store TTL in our caps cache (default 1d).
jon: metrics: caps_fetch_count, caps_fetch_failure, loader_path_selected, streaming_bytes_wasted (counts bytes pulled but discarded due to verification failure).
anya: QA: add a canary mode REDWOOD_COMPRESSION_HANDSHAKE=v2 that enables caps fetch for select accounts. also add stress tests that upload mixed gzipped/uncompressed shards and race cold-hot restarts.
sasha: dev note: index writers need to be updated to optionally emit v1 mapping with `chunks: [{tensor: "wte", blob: "shard-1", off: 123, len: 456, compressed: true}]`. this avoids complex guessing in runtime.
kevin: fallback semantics: if loader selects mmap-first and that fails due to mismatch, it should gracefully degrade to streaming-first rather than erroring the whole model load. track as a non-fatal fallback_count metric.
anya: docs: add a short page to model onboarding checklist about preferred uploader settings: prefer multi-chunk raw offsets for mmap workloads, or include .caps.json if compressing.
claire: security: treat .caps.json as unsigned until we wire signature. don't rely on it for critical auth decisions. always verify binary signature before trusting offsets for mmap.
jon: edge-case: small objects might still be gzipped by intermediate proxies. loader should treat an unexpected gzip signature at byte 0 as a runtime mismatch and trigger fallback, not crash.
sasha: testing: add unit tests for loader path selection + a fuzz harness that truncates headers, removes .caps.json, and flips compression flag.
kevin: ops: add an alert if fallback_count spikes > 5% over baseline and a runbook entry for "compression mismatch warmup failures".
anya: plan: I'll sketch a short RFC with example .caps.json schema, index v1 sketch, required metrics, and a migration checklist. pinging @matt to own the RFC?
claire: tagging infra: this will touch the uploader CLI and our catalog writer - heads-up.
dev-bot: RFC draft created: /r/compression-handshake-v2 (pinned to #eng-ml). :white_check_mark:
anya: thanks all — I'll drop the link and a canary rollout plan in the thread. :thumbsup:
